title: fanout orchestration and result hydration for multi-tool executions
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Improves multi-tool call ergonomics by routing parallel invocations via a controlled fanout conductor, injecting tool results deterministically into the response stream and adding best-effort retry semantics. Backwards-compatible for OpenAI compatibility layer; opt-in structured-output strict mode introduced.
description: Motivation: customers are composing multiple tools (search, exec, db-read) in a single turn and need predictable ordering of injected results in streaming mode, bounded latency under partial failures, and clear integration with the OpenAI-compatible call surface. Summary of changes: add a lightweight FanoutConductor in the runtime dispatcher that orchestrates parallel tool invocations, collects results, and performs deterministic hydration of tool outputs into the token stream or final structured payload; introduce a retry policy abstraction with idempotency hints for tools; extend the OpenAI-compat layer to accept concurrent tool call arrays and a new 'structured_output_mode' flag (loose|strict) for validating injected payloads; expose a small SDK ergonomic helper in TS/Python to declare multi-tool call graphs and per-tool retry semantics. Design notes: the conductor issues concurrent requests with a soft concurrency cap per-request, tracks tool-level idempotency tokens and causal ordering metadata, and can emit partial injection updates to the streaming wire when downstream clients opt into "hydration streaming". Retires the previous ad-hoc injection code paths in runtime/exec and replaces them with a single deterministic merge function that preserves declared call order unless explicit reordering is requested. Compatibility: OpenAI-compatible responses continue to work with single-tool call patterns; when callers submit multiple tool calls using the new array form, the compatibility shim will translate old fields to the new structure and set structured_output_mode=loose by default. Migration and rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag fanout_conductor (disabled by default for enterprise Private installs); gradual rollout to hosted fleet with canary on 10% traffic, monitor token-latency and injection-error-rate dashboards. Testing: added unit tests for conductor state machine, end-to-end integration tests exercising streaming hydration, and chaos tests that simulate partial tool failures and network flakiness; added doc examples and a migration note. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (ENG-1029) [x] unit + integration tests [x] SDK ergonomic helper implemented (TS/Python) [x] docs + migration note [x] canary rollout plan prepared.

review_comments: Marco Liang: Overall looks good; main concern is ensuring we don't increase tail latency when one slow tool blocks hydration. Please add a hedging/timeout strategy and unit coverage.
Aisha Patel: Added soft concurrency cap + hedging timeout (configurable) and unit tests for hedging behavior in test_multi_tool_hydration.py.
Evan Kim: Can we avoid breaking existing streaming clients that expect token-by-token increments? How will partial hydration behave over SSE/HTTP2?

Aisha Patel: By default we keep tokenized streaming identical for single-tool flows. For multi-tool flows we emit explicit 'injection' events separated in the stream; clients that don't understand them will ignore (fields are additive). Added docs and a compatibility note. Also added a 'hydration streaming' opt-in flag.
Sofia Ruiz: Security: ensure auth tokens aren't leaked when tools rehydrate traces; audit logs should mask sensitive tool outputs by default.
Aisha Patel: Audit masking added to telemetry hooks; updated privacy tests to assert redaction on known sensitive tool types.
Evan Kim: Approve after the canary gating and dashboard thresholds are verified in staging.
Marco Liang: Approve - tested canary run and observed no regression in P50/P95 token latency on our internal test harness.

post_merge_tasks: Enable fanout_conductor on 10% hosted traffic (canary), monitor 'injection-error-rate' and 'fanout-queued-time' dashboards; coordinate with support for SUP-324 customers who reported multi-tool quirks.
notes_for_release: This change improves multi-tool ergonomics and should reduce developer friction for complex call graphs; recommend announcing structured_output_mode to SDK users and providing the migration snippet in the release notes.
migration_steps: 1) Enable feature flag in staging and run canary traffic; 2) Update SDK to latest to use multiTool helpers; 3) For Private installs, coordinate a config flip with the support team; 4) Monitor dashboards and be ready to disable flag if injection-error-rate > 0.5% or fanout-queued-time regresses > 30%.
user_impact_summary: Most users will be unaffected unless they adopt multi-tool arrays or the strict structured output mode. Early adopters will gain deterministic injections, clearer error semantics for partial failures, and better retry behavior for idempotent tools.
